Two children named but not yet cast: idle-detection-trigger, token-rotation-mechanism. No code written to cairn/ — the cairn device (devices/cairn/) does not exist yet.

open_threads: The cairn device (devices/cairn/) is the unbuilt foundation this ticket depends on.

Four hidden assumptions surfaced at /intent and still standing: (1) idle detection mechanism undesigned ('3 hours without a human' screensaver trigger — the mechanism itself is a child), (2) alpha order assumed sufficient (no device priority), (3) single serial pass assumed sufficient before system wakes, (4) announce feed assumed correct channel vs. dedicated bus channel. All measurable once the first sleep cycles run.

Key design ruling from this session to carry: the probe is the pattern, not the class. A three-line custom probe (match, decide, forward) is valid — no shim, no bus routing, no LLM. Akien: 'it's also ok to custom code a probe with just the tiny fragment of code above and not even bother its shim.'

Held-out devices (benched by the heartbeat) were discussed but not fully resolved — the probe fires on bus messages regardless of bench status, so the current answer is 'their probe forwards like anyone else's.' Not yet tested.
